limits: Five services are the repetition units. No old service is pooled and no per-position observation is an independent service replicate.
PID storage read_bytes, logical rchar, cgroup I/O and partition device counters remain separate; device background traffic and parent disks are never added or attributed to expert SSD reads.
I/O envelopes include client launch/teardown. Eleven quality HTTP windows share one controller envelope and have no per-question I/O.
Missing samples, PSI, counter resets, cgroup plateaus and bracket uncertainty remain explicit unknowns; no interpolation or fake zeros.
memory.current sampled peak and memory.peak charge peak are distinct service-lifecycle observations, each compared to 16GiB separately.
NVIDIA, cgroup, process and file-cache views overlap and have noncoincident peaks; physical RAM54GB stays INDETERMINATE.
This does not divide exclusive waiting time, establish pure observer overhead, or accept a performance improvement.
resources.integrity_limit: Raw/trace content hashes reused from terminal resource audit; final stat equality does not exclude same-metadata byte replacement.

HTTP.request_numerical_and_protocol_checks: Reused fixed audited group decisions; no re-analysis.

limits: No causal frequency for the old16 requests: observer can perturb worker ordering.
New entry opportunities and direct losses are exact bookkeeping, not a counterfactual decomposition of historical speed.
No old direct bound is assumed valid for new entry histories; no new counterfactual GPU/lower-cache replay.
Raw cumulative/nested timers and PID read bytes are not exclusive SSD/H2D waiting or expert-only storage traffic.
At most one future candidate; no optimization implementation or performance acceptance. Prior NO_GO/default-off and54GB unknown persist.
independent_review_limits: The 22/50365 (0.0436811278%) value is observed software READ event frequency in exactly eight new observer-on diagnostic decode requests; events and positions are not independent service replicates. It is neither a global counterfactual read-saving ceiling nor a speedup estimate.

The 4482 entry mirror candidate occurrences are accumulated across 97920 layer-plans (8 requests x 255 true decode forwards x 48 layers). They are not distinct experts or one request-entry cache inventory; 8 mirror slots per layer do not cap the accumulated occurrence count at 8 x 48.

The S/L identities are exact arithmetic in the new instrumented runs. Entry candidate opportunities depend on prior cache and scheduling history, including earlier writebacks; 470 and -2 at k1 are not independent causal shares of a counterfactual performance effect.

At k1 the 468 mirror deficit is 470 entry-opportunity difference minus 2 direct-loss difference; direct losses are S6 and L4. This local mechanism does not account for the main deficit. k0 has different prompt lengths, and k2/k3 mirror reversals remain included.

Twenty-two retained diagnostic witnesses establish successful actual READs after a same-plan reservation removed an entry-needed mirror opportunity. All are active at claim and later published. Changing victim protection can alter future history, replacement, traffic and execution time; it is only one frozen future candidate, not an implemented or accepted optimization.

The quality11 run contains three additional decode direct-loss witnesses and zero prefill direct losses. These observations remain in quality evidence and are not pooled into the eight-diagnostic-request frequency or decision population. All nineteen observer-on HTTP prefill phases recorded zero direct losses.

Old sixteen-request evidence is not pooled with these new requests, and old offline upper bounds are not transferred to new entry histories. Observer instrumentation can perturb worker ordering. On/off differences are descriptive single sequential service-cell observations, not pure observer overhead or stable performance effects.

The 117487546-byte resource report was read once by this review. Fifteen original raw resource files totaling 15229558 bytes reuse the completed reader SHA with unchanged dev/inode/size/mtime and complete-file/bytes-consumed receipts; twenty-four trace binaries reuse prior integrity hashes and unchanged signatures. No raw resource or route parsing/hash replay was performed here, and same-signature content substitution is not independently excluded.

Resource coverage is five service lifecycles, 27 HTTP timing windows and 17 client I/O envelopes. The eleven quality questions share one I/O envelope; no per-question storage attribution exists. PID storage read_bytes, logical rchar, cgroup and device counters remain separate; cumulative/nested times do not isolate SSD or H2D waiting.

Resource sampling retained 2368 samples, including 2140 scheduled GPU-observation skips. PSI and live file-cache peaks remain unknown; each service has 15 prelaunch cgroup-unknown records, and cgroup I/O disagreement remains. memory.current sampled excess and memory.peak charge excess peak at 233472 and 73728 bytes respectively, are separate observations, and memory.events.max is nonzero. Recorded OOM and swap are zero, not a whole physical-memory proof.

Prior performance NO_GO, candidate default-off, GEMM/precision and MTP/Phase-D constraints remain unchanged. Whole physical RAM54GB is INDETERMINATE; no new performance or numeric equivalence claim beyond frozen observer contract and HTTP evidence is made.

This is a completed-evidence independent review, not the final protection execution. Final protection has not been run by this reviewer; its own owned exit receipt and later documentation-only delivery identity still require closure.

owned_processes.limit: Only recorded owned PID/PGIDs; PID reuse also fails closed. This does not establish GPU or global idle.
